segment_text: 15.7 DEATH OR MENTAL INCAPACITY OF PRINCIPAL. If the Principal is a natural person, upon the death or mental incapacity of a Principal, the executor, administrator, or personal representative of such Principal shall transfer the Principal's interest in Franchisee to a third party approved by BKC within a reasonable time after the Principal's death or mental incapacity. Transfers by devise or inheritance shall not be subject to BKC's right of first refusal under Paragraph 15.4 above, but shall be subject to the same conditions imposed on any INTER VIVOS transfer under Paragraph 15.5 above. All other transfers shall be subject to BKC's right of first refusal under Paragraph 15.4 above, or if such right is not exercised, the same conditions as may be imposed on any INTER VIVOS transfer under Paragraph 15.5 above. In the case of transfer by devise or inheritance, if the heir is not approved or there is no heir, the executor shall use best efforts to transfer the Principal's interest to another party approved by BKC within twelve (12) months from the date of the Principal's death. If the conveyance of the Principal's interest to a party acceptable to BKC has not taken place within the twelve (12) month period, BKC shall have the option, to purchase the Principal's interest at fair market value.

annotator_notes:
§14.4 DRAFTING SESSION, 2026-09-16. Eligibility was RULED BY THE REVIEWER at v0.52 (§10.2, SPLITTING_EXCLUSION_INVESTIGATION.md Decision 3); this session drafts the item the ruling authorised and resolves the one question that ruling deliberately left open. The segment disposition moves PENDING_ANNOTATION -> ANNOTATED.

ACTION -- §8.8'S DECISION PROCEDURE WAS RUN EXPLICITLY, NOT ASSUMED, because v0.52 flagged it into this segment file as a question that must not be silently resolved. The real verb is "purchase" (recorded verbatim here per §8.8's requirement whichever way the answer goes). RULED DEFENSIBLY MAPPABLE to PROCURE -- see the new §8.8.3, which records the measurement. In short: `ACTIONS` holds no PURCHASE/BUY/ACQUIRE (checked by execution against the real 34-verb list, which is why the cold draft's PURCHASE/BUY/ACQUIRE set was not lockable); PROCURE is nearest AND denotes the same performance, obtaining the thing; and in THIS corpus 10 of the 12 `procure` sentences use exactly that obtain-a-thing sense, including outright buying ("additional merchandise procured by Agent", C06-064; "from import or from domestic procurement", E08-002). §8.8.2's two discriminators both come back negative: purchase and procure co-occur in 1 of 251 sentences and that one is a header-spliced fragment with the words in different grammatical roles, not two enumerated duties (contrast `defend`, used alone 33 times and added 58); and the extra element purchase carries, consideration at fair market value, is a differentia of MEANS, not a different act. §8.8's own accepted `arrange`->PROCURE is a looser fit than this one.

WHY THE ACCEPT-SET IS A SINGLETON, AND WHY THAT MUST NOT BE READ BACKWARDS. ["PROCURE"] is single because §3.4 asks for every TAXONOMY verb a competent annotator could defend and no second member clears -- PAY does not compose with this item's own object_class ("pay the Principal's interest" is not what the span says) and TRANSFER names the executor's side of the conveyance, not BKC's. It is NOT single because §8.8's genuine-gap rule fired. It did not. There is no action_not_in_taxonomy tag on this item.

DENOMINATOR CONSEQUENCE, STATED BECAUSE IT IS A PUBLISHED-FIGURE DECISION AND NOT A DRAFTING DETAIL. known_gaps is EMPTY, so under §9.1 this item belongs in criterion 2's IN-FORCE denominator (len(known_gaps) == 0). Had `purchase` been ruled a genuine gap it would have carried action_not_in_taxonomy and stayed out. Marginal effect in isolation: +1 denominator, +0 numerator -- 3/9 = 33.3% would become 3/10 = 30.0%. IT DOES NOT MOVE TODAY, and the reason is recorded under SCOREABILITY below rather than left to be rediscovered.

SCOREABILITY, AND A DELIBERATE CHOICE NOT TO BACKDATE. This item is stamped v0.53. C11-094's three cassettes are stamped v0.28 (read directly off evals/cassettes/gold/C11-094/run*.json), so under F16's per-item staleness check (run_scoring.runs_for_item) this item is CASSETTE-UNSCOREABLE and is disclosed by report.py's G8, exactly as C17-02 already is after the F13 restamp. Stamping it v0.28 to force a cassette match was considered and REJECTED: it is precisely the move §22.1's own "what must NOT happen" list forbids, and it would be false besides -- §2.5 (v0.39), §2.5.1 (v0.41), §10.2 (v0.52) and §8.8.3 (v0.53) are all rules this item was annotated under and none existed at v0.28. The cost is that the +1 above is realised only when C11-094 is re-recorded at §10's freeze pass. Confirmed by execution, not predicted: the scoring run after this item was added still reports in-force criterion 2 = 3/9 and all-items = 5/15, with C11-02 named in the G8 disclosure.

PREDICTION DISCLOSURE, PRE-REGISTERED AT v0.52 BEFORE THE ELIGIBILITY RULING AND REPEATED HERE PER §10.2 PART 3. openai/gpt-oss-120b emits a candidate at this span on 1 of 3 recorded runs (run 2 only, MAY PURCHASE). Under §6's modal rule the item's outcome is therefore MISSED. Adding it can only LOWER criterion 2, which is the monotone direction §10.2 permits. Note the emitted verb PURCHASE is off-taxonomy and would fail clause 2 against any legal accept-set, so this ruling's choice between PROCURE and a tag does not change this item's outcome -- only which denominator it is counted in.

MODALITY MAY, decided by citation rather than re-derived: §3.2's "is entitled to / is permitted to" row, and locked item C13-03 is the direct precedent -- "Either party shall have the right to terminate" is annotated MAY. "shall have the option, to purchase" is the same entitlement shape; the leading "shall" governs the HAVING of the option, not a duty to buy. §3.3 forbids an accept-set here. §2.5.1 is explicit that the modal decides modality but not eligibility.

OBLIGOR "BKC", which RESOLVES: evals/registry/C11.json registers it as an alias of "Burger King Corporation" with exactly this casing (§21 R2's case-sensitivity trap checked, not assumed). obligor therefore does NOT appear in missing_fields.

OBLIGEE ABSENT, with both alternatives considered and recorded rather than silently dropped. "a party acceptable to BKC" sits inside the condition and denotes the transferee whose failure to appear TRIGGERS the option -- the party BKC's purchase displaces, not one the option runs to. "the executor" is in the neighbouring sentence, and §3.5 forbids importing a party from outside the span; §3.5's v0.41 test held that even an unambiguous in-segment anaphoric antecedent does not satisfy the in-span requirement. §3.5.4 governs and its own warning applies squarely: obligee assignment is modality-independent, but that is NOT a licence to invent a counterparty for a MAY.

OBJECT_CLASS. §3.6's REQUIRED enumeration 1 names "the Principal's interest in Franchisee" -- this segment's own phrase -- as its worked example and demands BOTH nominal anchors, so the set carries the possessor anchor (principal_interest, which is what THIS span actually says; the span does not name the thing owned, unlike C11-01's) and the thing-owned anchors (franchise_interest, franchisee_interest, ownership_interest, equity_interest). Five entries, inside §3.6's 3-6 band, no number-padding. §3.6.1 CHECKED rather than waved through, because "principal_" looks like a party prefix: it is not this item's obligor (BKC) or obligee (ABSENT), so carve-out 2 clears it, and "the Principal's interest" is the object's own name in the span, which carve-out 1 independently clears. §3.4's freeze-pass queue note: C11-01 is queued for widening to principal_interest as item F1 and IS NOT WIDENED HERE -- this is a new item authored fresh at authoring time, not a widening of a locked one.

TEMPORAL null, and this is NOT a §8.6/§8.6.1 call. The obligation carries no timing phrase of its own: "within the twelve (12) month period" sits inside the quoted condition and says when the CONVEYANCE had to happen, not when BKC must exercise the option. §3.7's "temporal = null only when the obligation genuinely carries no timing phrase" is satisfied on its own terms. §8.6.1's v0.52 principle -- null marks what the IR cannot REPRESENT, never what the classifier cannot REACH -- is not engaged in either direction here, because there is no timing phrase for the duty at all to represent or to reach. No within_preposition tag and no §8 parenthetical-numeral claim is asserted for this item.

CONDITIONS -- ONE entry. §17.1's diagnostic counts scoping markers and there is exactly one ("If") governing the whole circumstance; §3.8.2 Rule A sets the quote extent, running from the marker to just before ", BKC shall have". The embedded "within the twelve (12) month period" stays verbatim inside the condition per §17.2 -- an entry containing further material is the correct answer, not a clause-7 failure. §3.8.3 is not engaged (no redundant restatement), so no conditions_accept_set.

UNDERSPECIFIED true on §3.9 trigger 1, from the ABSENT obligee alone; missing_fields ["obligee"]. Not over-determined here, unlike C11-01: BKC resolves and temporal is null, which §3.9 states explicitly is never a trigger.

REVIEWER-APPROVED 2026-09-17, as drafted, with the three flagged calls each settled EXPLICITLY rather than by silence: (1) the singleton action_accept_set is KEPT -- the drafter flagged that this puts an item in §9.1's in-force denominator that is near-certain to fail clause 2, and that cost is accepted rather than cured by a widening made after the prediction was known (§3.4's justification test forbids that; the freeze pass remains the venue if the set is later judged under-scoped from the sentence alone); (2) the sibling divergence on primary object_class is accepted as TEMPORARY -- C11-01 is `franchise_interest` and C11-02 is `principal_interest`, and the two converge once C11-01's already-queued §10.1 F1 widening lands; (3) conditions: [] is CONFIRMED, and that ruling is generalised into §3.8 with a cross-reference at §2.5.1 (v0.54) -- a reviewable-standard phrase governs HOW a right is exercised, not WHETHER the obligation applies, so it is not a conditions entry. guideline_version stays v0.53 DELIBERATELY: the v0.54 rule CONFIRMS this item's existing treatment rather than changing it, and restamping a confirmed item is the gratuitous conforming event §22.1 and C11-01's own record-only correction both refuse. Calls (1) and (2) are C11-02's; recorded on both items so neither is read in isolation.
